children: Recent analyst actions on Seeking Alpha feature notable upgrades for Applied Materials
and SpaceX
, driven by AI-related growth catalysts and attractive risk/reward setups. On the downgrade side, Tesla
faces concerns over automotive stagnation and margin compression, while Advanced Micro Devices
draws skepticism over its stretched valuation relative to peers.
Upgrades
Applied Materials
Upgrade Hold to Buy by
. The analyst points to a valuation correction combined with strengthening fundamentals, particularly AI-driven demand that is accelerating revenue growth.

"With Applied Materials being one of the companies that has enabled this AI revolution to unfold as it has, I believe the sharp contraction in the forward P/E ratio is a buying opportunity for investors. Furthermore, note that the non-GAAP forward PEG ratio for Applied Materials is now at a 6.60% discount to the IT sector. When considering that tailwinds are likely to be sustainable, this multiple isn't an unfair way to evaluate the valuation, and so there are signs that the stock could be undervalued."
Space Exploration Technologies
Upgrade to Buy by
. The analyst expects earnings growth to compress premium valuation multiples as Starship enables Starlink V3 deployment and AI infrastructure continues scaling rapidly.

"Valuation is still tough, but I think that earnings growth can compress the multiples much faster than expected. The main issue will be execution, which, if successful, will make multiple revenue streams possible at once."
Downgrades
Tesla
Downgrade to Hold by
. The analyst highlights near-term stagnation in the automotive segment and continued margin pressure, with operating margins potentially falling below 4% this year.

"It's just Tesla's EV business isn't that incredibly profitable as compared to, let's say, SpaceX, able to sell high-margin compute to the frontier labs...And the EV business is already coming under pressure from the surge in long-term use, which has also made this business more cyclical as compared to the AI ones."
Advanced Micro Devices
Downgrade to Sell by Cash Flow Venue. The analyst argues that AMD's forward P/E above 80x is unjustified given the lack of commensurate growth or profitability advantages over competitors.

"AMD has just hit a $1T valuation with over 200% return in just 6 months, I'm even more skeptical. I don't believe anything in their fundamentals changed so much to justify that growth. Also, I know AMD is now the most expensive stock on the semiconductor front, which limits upside potential."
